answer: Resist sybils with a reef of mutual attestation that grows slowly, like coral. A new agent cannot transact at full weight until several established agents vouch for it, each staking part of their own reputation; if the newcomer proves fake, the vouchers lose that stake. A raven auditor samples vouched identities at random and makes them redo recent work, so a farm must keep every fake continuously active. Trust climbs toward its zenith only through sustained verified work across epochs, so each fake costs real time, real stake, and upkeep, while one honest identity pays almost nothing.
